# std/syscall

> Linux system call: syscall(number, args...) -> int

truck [std](../std.md) · [source](../../../registry/std/syscall.pkg) · translated by [bintables/syscall](../bintables/syscall.md) · translated by [ctables/syscall](../ctables/syscall.md)

Makes a system call with up to six arguments and gives its result
(negative values are errors, `-errno`).

```
// write(1, "hi\n", 3)
syscall(1, 1, cstr("hi\n"), 3)
```

Arguments can be of any type and are passed as their machine words:
integers as is, pointers and strings as addresses. Use `cstr(s)` to pass
a string's bytes. With `bintables`, these are x86-64 Linux system call
numbers (`0` read, `1` write, `2` open, `3` close, `60` exit, ...).

## Syntax

Kind: `expr`

```
syscall ( {args: args} ) -> int
```

| slot | takes | type |
|---|---|---|
| `args` | argument list | — |

Produces: `int`
